samples.summary: Ancestor safety rule ignores ownership, so a foreign-owned (non-root) ancestor — including a world-writable *sticky* one — is accepted, leaving the predictable review base replaceable by that user
samples.evidence:
`unsafeBaseReason` deliberately applies the uid check only to the leaf (line 529: `if (leaf && ... stat.uid !== uid)`), and for ancestors accepts anything whose mode has no group/other write bit, plus an explicit exemption for sticky directories (line 545-551: `const forbidden = leaf ? 0o077 : 0o022; if ((stat.mode & forbidden) !== 0 && !(!leaf && (stat.mode & STICKY) !== 0))`). Two consequences on a shared machine, both reachable on the DEFAULT path `os.tmpdir()/wafflebase-self-review/<branch>-<hash>` (spec-to-pr.mjs:723-727):

(1) Sticky does not restrain the directory's OWNER. POSIX sticky only says an entry may be removed/renamed by the entry's owner, the DIRECTORY's owner, or root. An attacker (uid 1001) pre-creates `/tmp/wafflebase-self-review` mode 1777 owned by themselves — any user may set the sticky bit on their own directory. `mkdirSync(base, {recursive:true, mode:0o700})` (line 836) then creates our leaf inside it; the leaf is ours and 0700 so the leaf check passes, and the ancestor check passes because `(0o1777 & 0o022) != 0` is excused by the STICKY branch. The attacker, as owner of that sticky directory, may still rename our leaf away and put a directory or symlink of the same name in its place at any point after the check — every subsequent `writeFileSync(diffFile...)` (line 941) and every `readFileSync(.../verdict.json)` (lines 761, 783) then lands on / comes from attacker-controlled storage.

(2) Mode bits on a directory you do not own are attacker-mutable. An ancestor owned by another non-root user at 0755 passes (`0o755 & 0o022 === 0`), yet that user can `chmod 0777` at any moment and replace our directory; the guard runs once, before the panel's multi-minute run.

The file's own docblock (lines 505-509) states the impact: the review directory holds the branch diff, and `priorFindingsFor` reads `verdict.json` back into the next round's verifier prompt — "anyone who can write that path can put text into an agent session holding the developer's credentials and repo access". So this is source disclosure plus a prompt-injection channel. The unit tests only cover a ROOT-owned sticky ancestor (`spec-to-pr.test.mjs`: `anc(mode, uid = 0)` with `unsafeBaseReason(anc(0o41777), 501, {leaf:false}) === ""`), which is why the foreign-owner case is invisible. A fix would accept the sticky exemption (and any ancestor) only when `stat.uid` is 0 or our own uid.

samples.summary: Ancestors are validated on the realpath-resolved chain while every later read/write uses the unresolved path, so an attacker-owned symlink ancestor can be re-pointed after the check (TOCTOU)
samples.evidence: Line 851-855 resolves the base (`realpathSync(base)`) and then validates only the RESOLVED ancestors; the leaf symlink check at 842-845 covers the leaf alone. All subsequent I/O uses the unresolved `base`: `rmSync(path.join(base, name))` (869), `readdirSync(base)` (868/878/755), `writeFileSync(diffFile)` (941), and the verdict reads at 761/783. Vector on the default path: an attacker creates the symlink `/tmp/wafflebase-self-review -> /tmp` (in sticky /tmp they own their own entry, so this is permitted and only they can replace it). `mkdirSync` then creates `/tmp/<branch>-<hash>` owned by us at 0700 — the leaf check passes — and the resolved ancestor chain is just `/tmp`, root-owned 1777, which the ancestor rule explicitly accepts. Once the check is done the attacker re-points the symlink at a directory of their own; the panel then writes the branch diff there and, on the next round, reads `verdict.json` from attacker-controlled content straight into the verifier prompt (the injection channel the docblock at 505-509 names). The guard never re-validates, and the panel run is minutes long. Hardening would mean opening the base once (fd / O_NOFOLLOW-style handle) or re-comparing `realpathSync(base)` immediately before each round's writes, or refusing when any UNRESOLVED ancestor component is a symlink not owned by us or root.

samples.summary: `printable` neutralizes only C0/C1 controls; bidi overrides and zero-width characters in model output still reach the terminal report the developer uses to judge the branch
samples.evidence: `printable` (line 286-293) replaces `[�--]` and collapses whitespace, which defuses ESC/CSI and CR as the docblock intends. It does not touch Unicode bidirectional controls (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) or zero-width/invisible characters (U+200B, U+200E/F, U+FEFF). A lens summary is model output derived from the diff under review, so a diff crafted to steer a lens (or simply a hostile fork diff reviewed locally) can embed U+202E in a `summary` and have `renderBlockingFindings` (line ~318 onward, `lines.push(`      ${printable(f.summary)}`)`) render text that displays reversed or with hidden segments — e.g. making a critical finding read as something benign on the exact screen the developer uses to decide whether to stop looping. Same class of defence as the existing `neutral()` in rebuttal.mjs; extending the character class (or stripping anything in the bidi/format categories) closes it.

samples.summary: Model-controlled text can suppress a real blocking finding from the local report and the carry-forward via the legacy infra shape rule
samples.evidence: `blockingFindingsIn` (spec-to-pr.mjs:791-800) now renders the developer-facing report through `carryForwardFindings`, whose final filter is `isInfraRecord` (prior-findings.mjs:56-61). After the projection strips the producer-set `infra` flag, the only branch that can still fire is the LEGACY one: no `file` and `summary.startsWith(INFRA_SENTINEL)`. Both of those are model output. A lens output (steerable by text in the diff under review) that omits `file` and begins its summary with "Review could not run — Claude API/quota error" is therefore dropped from the report AND from every later round's `--prior-findings`; the developer instead sees `no finding recorded (the lens may not have run)` (spec-to-pr.mjs:~305). The lens's own conclusion still blocks that round, so this is a display/recall weakness rather than a gate bypass, but the wording actively invites the reader to treat the round as infra noise and override it. The prefix branch is documented as removable once pre-flag PRs are closed; on the local path, where the flag is always stripped first, the branch buys nothing and only carries this risk.

samples.summary: A local squatter can deny self-review entirely, and does it through an uncaught EACCES rather than the guard's refusal path
samples.evidence: `mkdirSync(base, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` at line 836 runs before any validation and is not wrapped in try/catch, unlike every other filesystem call in `cmdReview`. Any local user can pre-create `/tmp/wafflebase-self-review` (the predictable base from `reviewBase`, line 723-727) mode 0700 owned by themselves; every developer on that host then gets an unhandled `EACCES` stack trace instead of the deliberate `refusing to use the review directory …` message, and `/self-review` — documented in `.claude/commands/self-review.md` and CLAUDE.md as the only machine review an ordinary branch gets — cannot run at all. The failure direction is safe (nothing is written), but it is a durable denial of the review path and the message does not tell the developer that a squatted directory is the cause. Catching the mkdir error and reporting it through `fail()` with the same wording as the guard would make the squat visible.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as the reviewer describes. In scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs, `unsafeBaseReason` applies the uid/ownership test only when `leaf` is true (line 529), and the ancestor branch is a mode-only rule with an unconditional sticky exemption (lines 545-551): `const forbidden = leaf ? 0o077 : 0o022; if ((stat.mode & forbidden) !== 0 && !(!leaf && (stat.mode & STICKY) !== 0))`. The ancestor walk at lines 855-862 is the only ancestor validation and calls it with `{ leaf: false }`, so a foreign-owned ancestor — including a non-root-owned 1777 sticky one — is accepted. `mkdirSync(base, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` (line 836) only sets 0700 on levels it creates, so a pre-existing attacker-owned `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review` (predictable default from reviewBase, lines 723-727) keeps its owner and mode. POSIX sticky restricts removal/rename to the entry owner, the DIRECTORY owner, or root, so the attacker who owns that sticky ancestor can still rename/replace our leaf after the one-shot check (TOCTOU), redirecting writeFileSync of the diff and the readFileSync of verdict.json at lines 761 and 783, whose contents priorFindingsFor (778-788) feeds into the next round's verifier prompt — the exact impact the file's own docblock states at lines 505-509 ("anyone who can write that path can put text into an agent session holding the developer's credentials and repo access"). Consequence (2) also holds: a foreign-owned 0755 ancestor passes yet can be chmod 0777'd after the check. No other guard closes this: realpathSync (line 853) resolves but does not pin, and the call-site comment at lines 819-823 shows the guard was explicitly meant to stop an attacker-owned intermediate. Tests only cover a root-owned sticky ancestor (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:641 `anc = (mode, uid = 0)`, line 654), so the foreign-owner case is untested, not handled. Real and in the security lane (TOCTOU/path substitution enabling source disclosure and prompt injection into a credentialed agent session).

verdict.reason: The described code is present and behaves as claimed. `reviewBase` (spec-to-pr.mjs:723-727) yields the predictable default `<tmpdir>/wafflebase-self-review/<branch>-<hash>`, whose intermediate component an attacker can pre-create in sticky /tmp. The leaf check at :840-845 lstats only the final component (intermediate symlinks are followed by lstat), and the ancestor walk at :851-862 iterates `ownedPathChain(path.dirname(resolved), ...)` over the realpath-RESOLVED chain, so the attacker's symlink component is eliminated before the symlink rejection in `unsafeBaseReason` (:521) can ever see it; the resulting resolved ancestor `/tmp` (mode 1777) is explicitly accepted by the sticky-bit exemption at :545-551. Every subsequent operation uses the unresolved path: `readdirSync(base)`/`rmSync(path.join(base,name))` at :867-870, `roundsOnDisk`/`priorFindingsFor` reads at :755-761 and :783, and `writeFileSync(diffFile/changedFile)` at :941-942 (dir derived from base at :890). No code re-validates `realpathSync(base)` or lstats the unresolved ancestors — `unsafeBaseReason`/`ownedPathChain` have exactly one call site (:844,:855,:860) — and the panel subprocess at :959-972 keeps a long window open. Impact is the injection channel the module's own docblock names at :505-509: attacker-controlled verdict.json fed into the next round's verifier prompt, plus branch-diff disclosure. This is squarely in the security lens (symlink/path TOCTOU, unsafe input into an agent prompt) and the gate reads as covering 'EVERY ANCESTOR' (:819-823) while missing the one attacker-supplied component, which the rubric treats as blocking.
